2608.11146.title: The Illusion of Cross-Lingual Safety in Low-Resource Languages
2608.11146.paper_summary: Safety alignment in large language models (LLMs) is largely developed in English, assuming these safeguards generalize across multilingual settings. However, this assumption remains underexplored and exposes a vulnerability in low-resource languages. We investigate cross-lingual safety transfer in four African languages, Twi, Hausa, Amharic, and Swahili, using LoDNA, a new safety dataset that pairs literal translations with culturally localized prompts. To move beyond generation-based evaluation, we propose a latent geometric framework that probes hidden-state refusal representations in LLMs. Our experimental results show that cross-lingual safety transfer is severely limited; harmful prompts retain less than 10% of the English refusal signal across most language-model pairs. Literal and localized prompts are semantically aligned (cosine 0.95-0.996) but drift across layers, suggesting models encode the concepts without routing them to safety mechanisms. These findings demonstrate that current multilingual safety alignment is superficial, providing strong evidence against the assumption of a universal, language-agnostic harm manifold within the specific low-resource languages studied. Warning: This paper contains example data that may be offensive or harmful.
2608.11146.paper_summary_zh: 安全對齊在大型語言模型（LLMs）中主要是在英語環境下發展的，假設這些安全措施可以在多語言環境中通用。<lb/>然而，這一假設仍然未被充分探討，並暴露了低資源語言中的一種脆弱性。<lb/>我們研究了四種非洲語言（Twi、Hausa、Amharic 和 Swahili）中的跨語言安全轉移，使用 LoDNA，一個新的安全數據集，將字面翻譯與文化本地化提示配對。<lb/>為了超越基於生成的評估，我們提出了一個潛在幾何框架，探查 LLMs 中隱藏狀態拒絕表示。<lb/>我們的實驗結果顯示，跨語言安全轉移受到嚴重限制；有害提示在大多數語言模型對中保留的英語拒絕信號不到 10%。<lb/>字面和本地化提示在語義上是對齊的（餘弦相似度 0.95-0.996），但在層之間漂移，這表明模型編碼了這些概念卻沒有將其路由到安全機制。<lb/>這些發現表明，目前的多語言安全對齊是表面的，為反對在所研究的特定低資源語言中存在普遍的、與語言無關的傷害流形的假設提供了有力證據。<lb/>警告：本文包含可能冒犯或有害的示例數據。
